nodes.description:
Hypothesis: the truncated protein binds or sequesters wild-type RDH12 and lowers total retinal reductase activity in the inner segment below the level one normal allele supplies. It rests on the suggestion, from the Drosophila photoreceptor ortholog, that RDH12 may act as a dimer; RDH12 dimerisation and mutant-wild-type interaction have not been shown.
Normal RDH12 function, which this hypothesis would reduce, is well characterised: the purified human enzyme has its highest catalytic efficiency for all-trans-retinal, and in rod inner segments it protects organelles against aldehyde toxicity from all-trans-retinal leaking out of the outer segment and from other aldehydes.

nodes.description: The initiating lesion is one of three single-base deletions clustered in the penultimate coding exon of RDH12: c.759del p.(Phe254Leufs*24), c.763del p.(Val255Serfs*23) and c.778del p.(Glu260Argfs*18). Each was found heterozygous and segregating with disease. The frameshifts lie downstream of the conserved cofactor-binding (residues 46 to 52) and catalytic (200 to 204) regions, which are left intact.

nodes.description: The clinical retinal disease: a rod-cone dystrophy that is milder and later in onset than recessive RDH12 disease. Rod function is affected first on electroretinography, and degeneration starts in the periphery, with bone spicules and vessel attenuation, while an island of central photoreceptors and good acuity persist. In the founding family the mean age at diagnosis was 28.5 years; in the British family the index patient had signs at about age 10. The circular autofluorescence ring around a residual foveal island resembles typical retinitis pigmentosa rather than the variegated macular atrophy of LCA13.

nodes.description: The premature stop codon falls within about 20 nucleotides of the last exon-exon junction, so the mutant transcript is predicted to escape nonsense-mediated decay. All three dominant frameshifts enter the same alternative reading frame and end in an identical novel C-terminal peptide (RGRRPACTAPWLRAWSP), replacing roughly 60 wild-type residues. Recessive truncations further downstream, such as c.806_810del, also escape NMD but do not create this peptide and are not dominant, which is why the peptide rather than truncation itself is suspected. In patient-derived organoids the mutant mRNA is present while total RDH12 expression is reduced by about 45 per cent, suggesting partial degradation; the mutant protein itself has not been detected separately from the wild-type protein.
